This factorization reduces variance by decoupling combinatorial receiver selection from continuous shot generation, enabling more stable estimation in sparse data regimes. The Group Convolution and Frame Averaging provide equivariant and invariant representations respectively, crucial for handling the permutation symmetry of players and the reflection symmetries of the pitch. Together these primitives form a minimal but complete foundation for translating complex football dynamics into verifiable, explainable models.
